text.p: Following are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Farooq Leghari and Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto discussed a number of issues, including those relating to domestic and foreign issues, during a meeting that lasted more than six hours.

- The death of a key police official in the killing of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother Murtaza Bhutto took a new twist when the official's family described it as a murder, denying the police version that it was a case of suicide.
- Five people, including two security personnel and a woman, were killed in a gunbattle between paramilitary troops and tribesmen near the city of Peshawar.
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif said he believed that the current year would be a year of change of the government.
- The Karachi Chamber of Commerce and Industry said it plans to develop and operate a new industrial estate in Karachi.

- The chairman of the Export Processing Zones Authority has said that more concessions in customs tariff would be needed to bring Pakistani export processing zones at par with other zones in the region.

- Pakistan will have a 8,157-megawatt electricity generation capacity by 1998/99 and 8,486 megawatts by the year 2002/03, an internal document of the state-run Water and Power Development Authority says.

- South Korea's Chebol Daewoo has reportedly given a firm indication of its willingness to form a consortium to aquire a 26-percent equity stake in the state-run Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto held an important meeting with Chief of the Army Staff General Jehangir Karamat soon after her six-hour meeting with the President Farooq Leghari on Saturday.
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif has said that nothing less than the dissolution of assemblies could solve the multiple problems being faced by the country.
- Pakistan and Lybia have signed an agreement to combat drug smuggling and terrorism.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, soon after her meeting with President Farooq Leghari on Saturday, consulted her legal adviser on some of the points raised in the meeting.
